items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: Joe Otkin, all those, that's what they played, the clarinets.

ctx.x: Could you tell us a little bit about the brass bands when you heard them when you were a boy? Did they sound about like the Eureka and the bands today, or were they a little different type, bigger or smaller? They were bigger.

You see, the bands then you take a manual prayer, cellist there, all the bands. They had baritone horns, and they had them alto horns, and mostly brass, and what is now, they Hollywood C saxophone, C malaphone and all that nice. And I would see saxophone clarinets. I mean, they was always big. They said, like, we used ten now, they had about fifteen, because it really actually was brass. Everything was brass. You see, outside the clarinets, they didn't have no sax. I mean, all the thing was brass, but the…
Did they mostly read music, or did some of them do like they do now? Strictly musicians.
